inline_comments.comment: Regression: `case 'day':` is missing from the topXAxis switch. The original code (visible in the removed `-` lines of this hunk) had all seven cases — millisecond, second, minute, hour, **day**, week, month. The new topXAxis switch skips straight from `case 'hour':` to `case 'week':`. Any diagram with `topAxis: true` and `tickInterval 1day` will now silently fall through the switch and not apply the custom tick interval on the top axis. The bottomXAxis switch correctly keeps `case 'day':` at line 695.

The guard against excessive tick counts can be silently bypassed when the time domain contains invalid dates. If either `minTime` or `maxTime` is an `Invalid Date` object (whose `.getTime()` is `NaN`), then `maxTime - minTime` evaluates to `NaN`. `Math.ceil(NaN / intervalMs)` is also `NaN`, and the check `NaN > MAX_TICK_COUNT` is `false` — so custom tick intervals are applied even with an invalid domain, which is exactly the crash scenario this PR aims to prevent. Fix: add `if (isNaN(timeDiffMs)) { return Infinity; }` immediately after line 622.

The comment on this line reads `// For all other formats, if dayjs strict parsing fails, throw an error`, but the code below does not throw — it logs a debug message and then falls through to `new Date(str)` for every format type, not just timestamp formats. The intended stricter behaviour (reject invalid dates for non-timestamp formats rather than falling back to `new Date()`) is documented but never implemented. This will mislead future maintainers, and the PR's own unit test at line 529 of ganttDb.spec.ts confirms the unintended fallback still occurs. Either implement the early-throw or remove the inaccurate comment.

`getEstimatedTickCount` is declared as a named function inside `draw()`, but it does not close over any variable from the outer scope — it only uses its own parameters and the module-level `dayjs`. Defining it inside `draw()` causes it to be re-created on every render call and makes it impossible to unit-test in isolation. It belongs at module scope alongside `MAX_TICK_COUNT`.

Inconsistent behaviour between the two axes: the bottom axis block (around line 676) emits a `log.warn` when `estimatedTicks > MAX_TICK_COUNT`, giving the developer a diagnostic message. The top axis block here silently skips applying the custom interval with no warning at all. Both axes should behave identically when rejecting an interval. This inconsistency is a direct consequence of the duplicated code (see general comments).

`isTimestampFormat` is declared with `const` inside `getStartDate`, meaning a new function object is allocated on every invocation of `getStartDate`. Since the helper closes over no outer-scope variables and is a pure function of its argument, it should be lifted to module scope (alongside other module-level helpers) to avoid the repeated allocation.

The comment `// Timestamp formats can fall back to new Date()` implies that only timestamp formats reach this line, but as noted above all format types fall through here. The comment directly contradicts the observed behaviour and the nearby `if (!isTimestampFormat(dateFormat))` block, which also takes a path for non-timestamp formats without throwing. The comment should be removed or corrected to `// All formats fall back to native Date parsing`.

This assertion depends on `new Date('202-12-01')` returning a Date whose `getFullYear()` is `202`. Three-digit year strings are not part of the ECMAScript date-time string format (which requires four-digit years), so parsing is implementation-defined. The same file already contains a comment at line 323 of ganttDb.js warning that 'WebKit browsers can mis-parse invalid dates to be ridiculously huge numbers'. On WebKit/Safari or a stricter engine this `new Date('202-12-01')` may return `Invalid Date`, causing the test to throw rather than return year 202, making this test non-portable. Consider asserting on an error being thrown for the malformed input, or pinning to a date string that is unambiguous across engines.

general_comments.comment: The entire tick-interval block — parsing, validating `every`, estimating tick count, and the seven-case switch — is copy-pasted verbatim between the bottomXAxis and topXAxis code paths. The duplication has already caused a concrete regression in this PR (the missing `case 'day':` on the top axis) and an inconsistency (bottom axis warns, top axis does not). Extracting a shared helper such as `applyTickInterval(axis, every, interval, weekday, domain)` would remove roughly 40 lines of duplication, make the logic easier to test in isolation, and ensure both axes always behave identically.

The PR description states the root cause was 'a Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) error'. TDZ is a specific JavaScript concept: accessing a `let` or `const` binding before its declaration within a block scope. No such access pattern exists in this diff — the actual problems were a lack of tick count validation in the renderer and inconsistent `new Date()` fallback for malformed dates. Using TDZ incorrectly in the commit message and PR description will mislead anyone searching the git history or issue tracker for the real root cause of #5496.
